title: introduce-browser-embedded-index-rag-playground-and-tool-shim
author: Priya Nair
commits: init: add browser rag playground skeleton
feat: implement wasm kNN shim and wasm-worker bridge
docs: add quickstart guide and troubleshooting
chore: add CI workflow for playground smoke tests
body:
Motivation: provide a minimal, offline-first RAG playground that demonstrates a browser-embedded vector index (WASM kNN) with a lightweight tool-calling shim to the Redwood API. Many quickstarts show server-side indexing or rely on cloud vector stores; this example shows how teams can prototype privacy-preserving clients that keep embeddings and nearest-neighbour search in the browser and optionally fall back to Redwood-hosted vector services when necessary.

What this PR does: adds a TypeScript React playground that: 1) embeds a small HNSW-like kNN implementation compiled to WASM, 2) runs a service worker/worker thread to manage index updates and query batching, 3) demonstrates on-device embedding caching and delta sync to a Redwood index, 4) includes a tool-calling shim that proxies redact/transform operations to the Redwood API with per-route budget controls, and 5) ships a step-by-step quickstart doc for local dev, CI smoke tests, and Android shim notes for offline-capable mobile wrappers.

Why it's useful: teams building privacy-sensitive RAG features often want to explore keeping document vectors client-side to reduce egress and surface an offline UX. This example documents tradeoffs (memory, serialization, cold-start), provides a safe default toy index (small dataset ~10–50 docs) and shows how to gracefully fall back to server-side retrieval when the browser index is stale or memory constrained. It also demonstrates tool-calling patterns (source attribution, cite-then-call, redaction hooks) that are practical for production integration patterns.

High-level changes and files: added a new examples/browser-rag-playground with: README quickstart, a minimal React UI, wasm worker that exposes add/query APIs, a browser-vector-shim for the TypeScript SDK showing embed+sync APIs, an Android shim README describing a small Kotlin wrapper that reuses the same sync protocol, and docs/quickstarts/browser-embedded-rag.md for the docs site. CI: added a playground-smoke workflow that builds the WASM, runs a headless smoke scenario and verifies basic end-to-end behavior.

Checklist: 
- [x] Playground skeleton and README
- [x] WASM worker kNN prototype with tests
- [x] TypeScript SDK shim example and integration snippet
- [x] Quickstart doc and troubleshooting notes for memory/timeouts
- [x] CI smoke workflow (build + headless test)
- [x] Android shim README and sample interop notes

Backward compatibility / migration notes: this is additive example code and documentation only. No runtime or SDK public API surface used in production is changed. If teams copy the shim into production, they should evaluate security (embedding material in client memory) and upgrade to server-side encryption and KMS integrations as required.

Related: references ENG-1427 (prototype client-embedded-indexing experiment), PM-321 (privacy-first RAG brief) and SUP-9182 (support ticket where a customer requested offline-first retrieval examples).

Testing: included unit tests for the wasm kNN glue, a headless smoke scenario that runs via Playwright and validates round-trip retrieval + tool call flow, and manual checklist for mobile interop testing.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on the examples/README clarity, the worker API surface and the fallback logic in the browser-vector-shim. WASM kNN is intentionally simple (not production HNSW): it is labeled experimental in the README and the docs note where to drop in a proper index (e.g., WebDNN/HNSWlib compiled targets).
review_conversation: Liam Park: Nice direction — two high-level asks: 1) add clearer signal for 'index staleness' in the UI and 2) document failure modes for large PDFs (OOM).
Priya Nair: Thanks — added staleness indicator state and updated README with OOM troubleshooting and recommended shard sizes. Also included a note on using chunking strategy to limit memory.
Sofia Martinez: Can you add a short note on security implications of storing embeddings in the browser and recommended encryption-at-rest strategies?
Priya Nair: Added a security subsection in the quickstart that recommends ephemeral indices, opt-in telemetry, and server-side KMS workflows for production deployments.
Daniel Ortega: CI is flaky on the first run due to wasm build caching on the runner — can we pin the wasm toolchain version or cache aggressively?
Priya Nair: Switched CI to use prebuilt toolchain cache and added retry step for the wasm build. Verified green on rerun.
Liam Park: Approving after addressing the items above.
release_notes: Add interactive browser-embedded RAG playground demonstrating WASM kNN index, client-side embedding caching, and tool-calling shim. Useful for prototyping offline-first or privacy-preserving retrieval UX.
